preterm-labor.core: Regular contractions with cervical change before 37 weeks; briefly delay eligible early births to improve neonatal outcomes, without prolonging unsafe pregnancies.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior spontaneous preterm birth, short cervix, multiple gestation, infection, smoking, uterine anomalies
Cervical surgery or prior painless second-trimester loss suggests cervical insufficiency

rows.label: Clues
items: Pelvic pressure, backache, increased discharge, contractions; assess membrane rupture and bleeding
Fever, uterine tenderness, fetal tachycardia → intraamniotic infection; maternal/fetal instability changes delivery timing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Premature inflammatory/uterine activation versus mechanically weak cervix with painless dilation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Sterile speculum examination** for pooling and cervix; ultrasound dates pregnancy and assesses presentation
Transvaginal cervical length; selected symptomatic cases: negative fetal fibronectin predicts low imminent birth risk
Collect GBS culture, urine studies; exclude previa before digital examination with bleeding

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Birth within 7 days, **24–33 6/7 weeks** → betamethasone; selected untreated 34–36 6/7-week pregnancies also eligible
★ Delivery expected <32 weeks → **magnesium sulfate** for neuroprotection, not primary tocolysis
Tocolysis: 48 hours for steroids/transfer; no maintenance; late-preterm steroids avoided with pregestational diabetes
★ **No tocolysis** with infection, significant abruption, severe preeclampsia, or fetal compromise; proceed toward delivery
Intrapartum penicillin for positive/unknown GBS; no routine antibiotics for intact membranes without infection

rows.label: Complications
items: Neonatal RDS, IVH, NEC, sepsis, cerebral palsy; magnesium toxicity → hyporeflexia, respiratory depression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Singleton short cervix ≤20 mm before 24 weeks → vaginal progesterone; consider at 21–25 mm
Cervical insufficiency/prior qualifying loss → cerclage; selected prior preterm birth plus short cervix also eligible
17-hydroxyprogesterone caproate no longer recommended; progesterone without short cervix does not prevent recurrence

rows.label: Mimics
items: Braxton Hicks: no progressive dilation
Cervical insufficiency: painless dilation, minimal contractions
PPROM: membrane rupture precedes labor; distinct latency-antibiotic pathway

rh-alloimmunization.name: Rh alloimmunization
rh-alloimmunization.scope: Rh(D) and other red cell alloimmunization (Kell, Duffy), anti-D immune globulin prophylaxis, indirect Coombs titer monitoring, fetomaternal hemorrhage (Kleihauer-Betke), middle cerebral artery Doppler for fetal anemia
rh-alloimmunization.core: Maternal IgG against fetal red-cell antigens crosses the placenta, causing fetal anemia, hydrops, and neonatal hemolysis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Antigen-negative mother/positive fetus; prior pregnancy, transfusion, bleeding, trauma, invasive procedures
Anti-D, anti-Kell, and anti-Duffy clinically significant; ABO incompatibility usually milder

rows.label: Clues
items: Often asymptomatic mother; fetal ascites, skin edema, placentomegaly, cardiomegaly
Neonate: early jaundice, pallor, reticulocytosis; severe disease → cardiovascular collapse

rows.label: Pathophys
items: First exposure sensitizes; subsequent antigen exposure produces an anamnestic response
Kell antibodies additionally suppress erythropoiesis; low titers can still cause severe disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ First prenatal visit: ABO/Rh type + **indirect Coombs**; repeat before routine antenatal prophylaxis
Identify antibody → fetal antigen status, serial titers; neonatal **direct Coombs** detects RBC-bound antibodies
★ Critical titer, often **1:16**, or previously affected pregnancy → middle cerebral artery Doppler
MCA peak systolic velocity >1.5 MoM → fetal blood sampling; Kell warrants specialist surveillance
Kleihauer-Betke quantifies hemorrhage for dosing: **300 µg covers 30 mL fetal whole blood**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe preterm fetal anemia → **intrauterine transfusion**; near term → delivery
Neonatal hyperbilirubinemia → phototherapy; severe hemolysis → exchange transfusion

rows.label: Complications
items: High-output heart failure, stillbirth, bilirubin encephalopathy, delayed neonatal anemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Unsensitized Rh-negative mother: **anti-D immune globulin** at 28 weeks and within 72 hours postpartum
Postpartum prophylaxis only with Rh-positive/unknown infant; also after sensitizing events; adjust dose for hemorrhage
★ Established anti-D sensitization → prophylaxis ineffective; no equivalent prophylaxis for Kell/Duffy
ACOG 2024: routine Rh testing/prophylaxis may be forgone for abortion/loss before 12 weeks

rows.label: Mimics
items: Parvovirus: nonimmune hydrops with negative maternal antibody screen
ABO hemolysis: may affect first pregnancy; fetal hydrops uncommon

rh-alloimmunization.evidence: Prophylaxis checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG Rh guidance](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/the-rh-factor-how-it-can-affect-your-pregnancy), [2024 update](https://doi.org/10.1097/AOG.0000000000005733); remaining content established teaching.

routine-prenatal-care.name: Routine prenatal care and early pregnancy
routine-prenatal-care.scope: Pregnancy diagnosis (beta-hCG), initial prenatal assessment, routine first-trimester screening, aneuploidy screening
routine-prenatal-care.core: Confirm and date pregnancy, assess maternal risks, offer one aneuploidy-screening strategy or diagnostic testing, and arrange time-sensitive prenatal studies.

rows.label: Who
items: All pregnancies; review obstetric history, drugs, illness, substance use, violence, family history
Offer carrier screening and genetic counseling; discuss patient preferences and right to decline

rows.label: Start/stop
items: Early visit: urine hCG confirms pregnancy; serum quantitative hCG for uncertain/complicated cases
★ First-trimester **ultrasound crown–rump length** best establishes gestational age
Serum screen 10–13 6/7 weeks; NT 11–13 6/7; cfDNA from 10 weeks

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Initial **CBC, ABO/Rh, antibody screen, urine culture**; HIV, syphilis, HBsAg, HCV, rubella immunity
GC/chlamydia by age/risk; offer one aneuploidy strategy regardless of maternal age
Anatomy ultrasound 18–22 weeks; AFP for open neural tube defects when not otherwise assessed

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Abnormal screen → counseling, ultrasound, **CVS/amniocentesis** before irreversible decisions
CVS: 10–13 weeks; amniocentesis: ≥15 weeks; neither automatically required after negative screening
Rh-negative, unsensitized → anti-D prophylaxis at 28 weeks and after sensitizing events

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **cfDNA is screening**, not diagnostic; does not screen open neural tube defects
Single hCG value cannot establish viability or location; pain/bleeding → ectopic evaluation
Folate before conception/early gestation; avoid alcohol, tobacco, teratogens; no live vaccines

septic-pelvic-thrombophlebitis.name: Septic pelvic thrombophlebitis
septic-pelvic-thrombophlebitis.scope: Ovarian vein thrombosis, deep septic pelvic thrombophlebitis, persistent postpartum fever, unresponsive to broad-spectrum antibiotics, CT with IV contrast, therapeutic anticoagulation and IV antibiotics
septic-pelvic-thrombophlebitis.core: Persistent spiking postpartum fever despite adequate broad-spectrum antibiotics suggests infected pelvic venous thrombosis after other sources are excluded.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cesarean delivery, postpartum endometritis, pelvic surgery, prolonged labor, maternal hypercoagulability
Right ovarian vein more often involved because of anatomy and venous stasis

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Fever persisting **48–72 hours or longer** despite treatment, with relatively well appearance between spikes
Ovarian vein involvement may cause flank/lower abdominal pain; deep pelvic branch disease may be painless
Tachycardia and tenderness variable; blood cultures often negative, especially after antibiotics
Dyspnea, pleuritic pain, hypoxemia → assess pulmonary embolism

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Venous endothelial injury, postpartum stasis, and hypercoagulability produce thrombus with local infection
Infected clot remains an inflammatory focus despite initially suitable uterine antibiotic coverage

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast**: enlarged thrombosed ovarian vein or pelvic venous filling defect
MRI alternative when CT unsuitable; small pelvic branch thromboses may evade imaging
Reassess wound, urine, breasts, blood cultures; ultrasound/CT for retained products or pelvic abscess
Imaging-negative deep disease remains exclusion diagnosis; fever response to heparin is not a definitive diagnostic test

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Continue **IV broad-spectrum antibiotics**, e.g., clindamycin + gentamicin; add ampicillin for enterococcal concern
★ Confirmed symptomatic ovarian vein thrombosis → **therapeutic LMWH/UFH** plus antibiotics
Postpartum provoked ovarian vein thrombosis often anticoagulated about 3 months; extend if persistent risks
Imaging-negative deep SPT: anticoagulation individualized; evidence weaker than classic empiric-heparin board teaching
Persistent illness → revisit resistant organisms, abscess needing drainage, or alternative noninfectious fever source

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary embolism, extension to renal vein/IVC, sepsis; anticoagulation-associated hemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Cesarean antibiotic prophylaxis, early mobilization, VTE-risk-based prophylaxis, prompt endometritis treatment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pelvic abscess: localized collection on imaging; source control needed
Retained products: bleeding, subinvolution, intrauterine material; evacuation when clinically indicated
Drug fever: temporal medication relationship, unrevealing source evaluation

septic-pelvic-thrombophlebitis.evidence: Anticoagulation checked 2026-10-30: [ASH postpartum ovarian-vein review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6142588/); imaging-negative practice uncertainty distinguished from classic board teaching.

sexual-assault.name: Sexual assault
sexual-assault.scope: Forensic examination, STI prophylaxis (ceftriaxone, doxycycline, metronidazole), HIV post-exposure prophylaxis, hepatitis B vaccination, emergency contraception, psychological counseling
sexual-assault.core: Trauma-informed care restores control: obtain separate consent for treatment, examination, evidence collection, and disclosure; prioritize immediate safety.

rows.label: Principle
items: Nonjudgmental language; explain each step, offer advocate/chaperone, permit stopping at any point

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Stabilize; offer **SANE exam**, preserve chain of custody; avoid treatment delay
Pregnancy test; site-specific STI NAAT; baseline HIV, HBV, syphilis serology

rows.label: Prophylaxis
items: ★ Adolescent/adult females: **ceftriaxone once + doxycycline/metronidazole for 7 days**
★ HIV substantial-risk exposure **≤72 hours** → 28-day PEP; never await source testing
Preferred PEP: **bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide**; check renal function/interactions

rows.label: Don't
items: Require police reporting, blame survivor, coerce examination, or promise absolute confidentiality

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Child/vulnerable-adult abuse, certain injuries → mandatory reporting; explain confidentiality limits
Prepubertal children → specialist testing; routine empiric STI prophylaxis generally deferred

rows.label: Follow-up
items: Results within 1 week; repeat HIV/syphilis tests, finish vaccines, arrange trauma-focused counseling
Ongoing danger/suicidality → urgent safety intervention; support survivor-directed reporting decisions

rows.label: Traps
items: Normal examination does not exclude assault; absent resistance or intoxication does not establish consent
Offer evidence collection despite bathing, clothing changes, or delayed presentation
Pregnancy → replace doxycycline with pregnancy-compatible chlamydia treatment, e.g., azithromycin

table.title: Additional prevention
rows: Offer ulipristal, levonorgestrel, or copper IUD

surgical-wound-complications.name: Surgical wound complications
surgical-wound-complications.scope: Superficial wound separation, fascial dehiscence (profuse serosanguineous drainage, emergent reclosure), evisceration (sterile saline dressings, emergency surgery), wound hematoma, wound seroma, surgical site infection
surgical-wound-complications.core: Postoperative wound drainage or separation requires determining whether fascia is intact; fascial failure is a surgical emergency even without exposed bowel.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, diabetes, malnutrition, smoking, glucocorticoids, wound infection, emergency/contaminated surgery
Vomiting, coughing, ileus or strenuous activity increase abdominal pressure on healing closure

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Sudden profuse serosanguineous drainage**, popping sensation, or new bulge → suspect deep disruption
Erythema, warmth, worsening pain, purulence → infection; systemic toxicity may precede visible skin changes
★ Pain out of proportion, crepitus, bullae, rapid progression → **necrotizing infection**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Early wound tensile strength depends on sutures; collagen remodeling later restores tissue support
Dead space permits fluid/blood accumulation; infection and poor perfusion impair collagen deposition

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Inspect/probe separated incision gently using sterile technique to assess **fascial integrity**
CBC, culture purulent drainage; systemic illness → blood cultures/lactate
Uncertain deep collection, stable patient → ultrasound/CT; obvious emergency → surgery without imaging delay

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Evisceration: sterile saline-moistened dressing**, supine, NPO, IV fluids, antibiotics, emergency operating room
Never force exposed bowel back through wound; surgical exploration determines viability and closure
Cellulitis alone → cefazolin/cephalexin; purulence → drainage, add antibiotics for cellulitis/systemic illness
Polymicrobial deep infection → piperacillin-tazobactam; add vancomycin for MRSA risk
Necrotizing infection → immediate debridement + broad IV antibiotics; antibiotics alone insufficient

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess, sepsis, bowel ischemia, incisional hernia; delayed healing and recurrent separation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Preincision antibiotic prophylaxis, sterile technique, glucose control, smoking cessation, adequate protein/calories

rows.label: Mimics
items: Contact dermatitis: pruritic geometric rash matching adhesive, no purulent drainage
Normal healing ridge: firm linear swelling without progressive pain, erythema, or systemic illness

table.title: Stable localized findings
rows: Observe; aspirate/drain if symptomatic or persistent
Small stable: observe; expanding: evacuate, control bleeding
Open/drain if needed, dressings, secondary closure/healing

surgical-wound-complications.evidence: Not checked online; established postoperative wound and emergency surgical management.

type-1-diabetes-mellitus.name: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
type-1-diabetes-mellitus.scope: Autoimmune islet destruction, honeymoon phase, diabetic nephropathy screening, microalbuminuria, intensive insulin
type-1-diabetes-mellitus.core: Autoimmune beta-cell destruction causing absolute insulin deficiency; onset at any age, sometimes initially mistaken for type 2 diabetes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Childhood/adolescent onset common but any age possible; family history, HLA-associated autoimmune susceptibility
Associated autoimmune thyroid disease and celiac disease; immune checkpoint inhibitors can cause insulin-deficient diabetes

rows.label: Clues
items: Polyuria, polydipsia, nocturia, weight loss, fatigue, blurred vision
★ **Vomiting, abdominal pain, Kussmaul breathing, dehydration** → evaluate DKA immediately
Honeymoon: temporary partial beta-cell recovery after diagnosis → lower insulin requirement, not cure

rows.label: Pathophys
items: T-cell-mediated islet destruction → impaired peripheral glucose uptake, hepatic glucose output and lipolysis/ketogenesis
Absent endogenous insulin → low C-peptide; glycemic variability worsened by inconsistent carbohydrate intake/exercise

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Symptoms + **random glucose ≥200 mg/dL**; otherwise A1c ≥6.5%, fasting ≥126, or 2-hour OGTT ≥200
Without unequivocal hyperglycemia/crisis → confirm with second abnormal result; never delay insulin in suspected DKA
GAD65, IA-2 or ZnT8 antibodies help classify uncertain cases; antibody negativity does not exclude
★ Adults: annual **urine albumin/creatinine ratio + eGFR after 5 years**; eye examination within 5 years
Albuminuria ≥30 mg/g: confirm 2 of 3 samples over 3–6 months; exclude exercise/infection-related elevations

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Basal-bolus insulin or pump + CGM**; carbohydrate-based mealtime dosing; automated delivery preferred when feasible
DKA → isotonic fluids, potassium-guided replacement, IV insulin after excluding severe hypokalemia
Typical adult A1c goal <7%, individualized for hypoglycemia/comorbidity; educate on insulin adjustment with activity
Hypoglycemia awake → rapid oral glucose; impaired consciousness → glucagon or IV dextrose
Hypertension + albuminuria → ACE inhibitor/ARB; no preventive RAAS blockade with normal BP/UACR/eGFR

rows.label: Complications
items: DKA, treatment-associated hypoglycemia; retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy, accelerated atherosclerosis
Repeated injections into same site → lipohypertrophy and erratic absorption

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Never omit basal insulin**; sick-day glucose/ketone checks, hydration, rescue glucagon and medical identification
Foot care, BP/lipid control, vaccination, injection-site rotation; TSH; celiac serology for suggestive symptoms

rows.label: Mimics
items: Type 2 diabetes: insulin resistance, usually preserved C-peptide; obesity does not exclude type 1
MODY: multigenerational young-onset diabetes, negative antibodies, preserved endogenous insulin
Diabetes insipidus: polyuria with dilute urine, normal glucose, often hypernatremia

type-1-diabetes-mellitus.evidence: Screening/diagnosis checked 2026-10-30: [ADA CKD Standards, 2026](https://doi.org/10.2337/dc26-s011); [ADA diagnosis Standards, 2026](https://diabetesjournals.org/care/article/49/Supplement_1/S27/163926); other care: established diabetes teaching.

urinary-incontinence.name: Urinary incontinence
urinary-incontinence.core: Involuntary urine leakage is classified by triggers, urgency, bladder emptying, and ability to reach a toilet; reversible contributors often coexist.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Childbirth, pelvic surgery, aging, obesity; diabetes, neurologic disease, prostate enlargement
Diuretics, sedatives, anticholinergics, constipation, infection, impaired mobility/cognition worsen control

rows.label: Clues
items: History: timing, volume, dysuria, weak stream, nocturia, fluid intake, obstetric/surgical and neurologic history
★ **New saddle anesthesia, leg weakness, retention** → urgent cauda equina evaluation
Continuous leakage after pelvic surgery suggests fistula; recurrent UTIs/hematuria require further investigation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Urethral support/sphincter failure, involuntary detrusor contraction, or impaired emptying produce distinct leakage patterns
Functional impairment can prevent continence despite intact lower urinary tract function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis + voiding diary**, focused pelvic/prostate and neurologic examination; review medications
Cough stress test with reasonably full bladder; assess prolapse, atrophy, fecal impaction
★ Suspected retention/emptying symptoms → **postvoid residual**; persistent >200 mL suggests inadequate emptying
No routine initial urodynamics/cystoscopy; uncertainty, hematuria, refractory symptoms → additional testing

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat reversible contributor; mixed incontinence → target most bothersome component
★ **Pelvic floor training/bladder training** underpin conservative care; weight loss, reduce caffeine, timed voiding
Urgency drugs: mirabegron or antimuscarinic; discuss cognitive risk and avoid antimuscarinics with retention
Mirabegron may increase BP; avoid severe uncontrolled hypertension; refractory urgency → botulinum toxin or neuromodulation
Genitourinary syndrome of menopause → local vaginal estrogen when suitable; not systemic estrogen for leakage

rows.label: Complications
items: Dermatitis, falls from rushing, social isolation, sleep disruption
Overflow → hydronephrosis/renal injury; bladder botulinum toxin → retention, UTI

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication review, accessible toilet, mobility aids; bowel regularity, maintain strength and weight

rows.label: Mimics
items: Polyuria: high urine volume from hyperglycemia/diuresis rather than primary storage failure
Vaginal fistula: constant leakage unrelated to voiding urge or exertion

urinary-tract-infections.name: Urinary tract infections
urinary-tract-infections.scope: Asymptomatic bacteriuria, acute cystitis, pyelonephritis, catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI), catheter removal, empiric antibiotics
urinary-tract-infections.core: Symptoms localize urinary infection: bladder disease lacks systemic illness; renal involvement causes fever or flank pain; bacteriuria alone is insufficient.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual activity, spermicides, pregnancy, obstruction/stones, urinary retention, instrumentation
Catheter duration, diabetes, prior resistant isolates or antibiotics increase complicated-course risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, frequency, urgency, suprapubic discomfort; absent vaginal discharge supports urinary source
★ **Rigors, CVA tenderness, vomiting, hypotension** → pyelonephritis or urosepsis
Catheterized patients: new urinary/systemic symptoms; cloudy urine or pyuria alone insufficient

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Usually ascending enteric bacteria, predominantly E coli; catheter biofilm maintains colonization
Urease-producing Proteus alkalinizes urine → struvite calculi and persistent infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis**: pyuria, leukocyte esterase, nitrites; negative nitrites do not exclude infection
Culture: pyelonephritis, pregnancy, CAUTI, recurrence/resistance; classic cystitis often clinical
Persistent fever after 48–72 hours, sepsis, or suspected obstruction → renal imaging
Asymptomatic bacteriuria: usually ≥100,000 CFU/mL; delirium alone → seek other causes without automatic antibiotics

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Treat asymptomatic bacteriuria only in pregnancy or before urologic mucosal trauma** in routine adult scenarios
★ CAUTI → **remove unnecessary catheter**; if needed and present >2 weeks, replace before culture/treatment
★ Infected obstructed collecting system → **urgent drainage + IV antibiotics**; antibiotics alone insufficient
Improving nonpregnant pyelonephritis: fluoroquinolone 5–7 days, other active drugs 7 days; high-risk cases individualized

rows.label: Complications
items: Bacteremia, septic shock, renal/perinephric abscess; pregnancy → preterm birth
Antibiotics → resistance, C difficile; fluoroquinolones → tendon injury, QT prolongation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid unnecessary catheters; closed drainage, daily removal assessment
Postmenopausal recurrence → vaginal estrogen; selected recurrences → postcoital/continuous antibiotic prophylaxis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vaginitis: discharge, pruritus, external burning
Urethritis: sexual exposure, discharge, positive gonorrhea/chlamydia NAAT
Bladder pain syndrome: chronic symptoms, repeatedly negative cultures

table.title: Initial antibiotics; tailor to culture/resistance
rows: Ciprofloxacin/levofloxacin; initial ceftriaxone if resistance risk
IV ceftriaxone; cefepime/piperacillin-tazobactam if Pseudomonas risk
Avoid nitrofurantoin/fosfomycin: inadequate renal tissue levels

vulvar-cancer.name: Vulvar cancer
vulvar-cancer.scope: Squamous cell carcinoma, melanoma of the vulva, lichen sclerosus malignant transformation, vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN), Paget disease of the vulva, staging, wide local excision, sentinel node biopsy
vulvar-cancer.core: Persistent vulvar pruritus with a focal ulcer, plaque, or mass requires biopsy, especially in an older patient.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HPV-related disease: smoking, immunosuppression; HPV-independent disease: older age, lichen sclerosus
Prior vulvar HSIL/VIN; chronic symptoms repeatedly treated without tissue diagnosis delay detection

rows.label: Clues
items: Nonhealing lesion, bleeding, dyspareunia, focal pain; enlarged inguinal nodes suggest regional spread
★ **Changing pigmented lesion** requires melanoma evaluation; amelanotic lesions also occur

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Squamous carcinoma spreads locally, then to inguinofemoral nodes; nodal involvement strongly influences prognosis
HPV-associated HSIL and HPV-independent differentiated VIN are distinct precursor pathways

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Punch/incisional biopsy** of suspicious lesion; sample viable edge, not only necrotic center
Document lesion size, depth, focality, proximity to midline; examine groin nodes
Suspicious nodes → ultrasound-guided sampling; advanced local extent → pelvic MRI and metastatic imaging
Stage by stromal invasion, adjacent-organ extension, and nodal/distant spread; evaluate multifocal disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized invasive disease → **wide local excision** with negative margins
Microinvasive SCC ≤1 mm stromal invasion generally needs no groin-node surgery
★ Unifocal **<4 cm**, invasion >1 mm, clinically negative nodes → sentinel-node biopsy
Larger/multifocal or node-positive disease → groin treatment; locally advanced → chemoradiation and/or surgery
Paget → excision; VIN → excision, or laser/imiquimod after excluding invasion

rows.label: Complications
items: Local recurrence, nodal metastasis; surgery/radiation → lymphedema, wound breakdown, sexual dysfunction

rows.label: Prevention
items: HPV vaccination, tobacco cessation; high-potency topical corticosteroids for lichen sclerosus, continued surveillance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lichen simplex chronicus: diffuse scratch-induced thickening; biopsy persistent focal changes
Candidiasis: yeast on microscopy, responds to antifungal; persistent lesion still needs sampling

table.title: Histologic clues
rows: Ulcerated/keratotic mass; HPV or inflammatory pathway
Asymmetry, irregular color/border; Breslow depth guides management
Chronic eczematous red plaque; intraepithelial glandular cells
